transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello Dr. Smith, I'm Shirley, and I can’t seem to stay focused long enough to get through all the reports and planning tasks my job requires anymore. I'm a healthcare manager and was promoted a couple of years ago, but despite working longer hours, I'm really struggling to keep up. My primary care doctor recently suggested that my lifelong focus difficulties might actually be undiagnosed ADHD, which is why I'm here today.

You mentioned these focus issues have been lifelong, but have you also noticed any persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest in things you usually enjoy, or excessive worry that have developed more recently alongside these work struggles?

I haven't really felt persistent sadness, a loss of interest in my hobbies, or excessive worry. Instead, I just feel incredibly stressed, overwhelmed, and exhausted from the constant, daily struggle to keep up with my work demands. It feels more like I'm constantly drowning in tasks rather than being depressed.
Besides difficulty focusing, do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or like you have an internal 'motor' that makes it hard to sit still for long periods?

No, I don't really experience physical restlessness, fidgeting, or feel like I have an internal motor driving me to move. My struggles are much more about my mental focus, drifting off, and trying to keep up with my tasks rather than physical hyperactivity.
Do you often find yourself frequently losing things, being forgetful in daily activities, or struggling to organize your tasks and work materials?

Yes, absolutely. Despite all my color-coded systems, I’m constantly misplacing essential things like my badge or meeting notebooks, wasting a lot of time retracing my steps. I also really struggle to organize my tasks, often starting a multi-step email request but completely forgetting the rest of the steps until someone chases me for it.
Do you often find that you are easily distracted by external stimuli, such as background noises or unrelated thoughts, when you are trying to complete your work?

I'm not really sure about being distracted by external noises, as that isn't something I've noticed much. However, my mind definitely drifts to unrelated thoughts quite a bit when I'm trying to focus. I haven't really tracked it clearly, but it's more of an internal drift than a reaction to background noise.
When you are working, do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or struggling to sustain your attention on tasks that are not particularly stimulating or interesting to you?

Yes, definitely. When I have to read long regulatory updates or draft complex plans, my mind drifts after just ten minutes and I find myself staring at the screen without absorbing anything. It is so mentally exhausting that I constantly avoid these tasks by checking my email or getting coffee instead of pushing through them.
Looking back at your childhood and school years, did you experience similar difficulties with organization, forgetfulness, or staying focused on tasks before the age of 12?

Yes, these issues definitely go back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers wrote on my report cards that I was smart but "daydreamed" and missed instructions. My parents actually had to sit with me at the kitchen table for hours because I would constantly lose track of what I was supposed to be doing on my homework.
